Let \(t=|x|\). Then the squared radius is
\[
r^2=f(t)=t^2+\left(\frac1{t-1}-1\right)^2
=t^2+\left(\frac{2-t}{t-1}\right)^2.
\]
For \(0\le t<1\), \(f'(t)>0\), so the minimum there is \(f(0)=4\).

For \(t>1\),
\[
f'(t)=2t-\frac{2(2-t)}{(t-1)^3}.
\]
Setting \(f'(t)=0\):
\[
t(t-1)^3=2-t
\]
\[
t^4-3t^3+3t^2-2=0=(t^2-2t+2)(t^2-t-1).
\]
The only real root with \(t>1\) is
\[
t=\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2}.
\]
Then
\[
r_{\min}^2=f(\phi)=\phi^2+\left(\frac1{\phi-1}-1\right)^2
=\phi^2+(\phi-1)^2=3.
\]
Since \(3<4\), this is the global minimum.

For a diameter \(AB\) of a circle centered at \(C=(0,1)\), write
\[
A=C+u,\qquad B=C-u,\quad |u|=r.
\]
Thus
\[
\overrightarrow{OA}\cdot\overrightarrow{OB}
=(C+u)\cdot(C-u)=|C|^2-|u|^2
=1-r_{\min}^2=1-3=-2.
\]

\[
\boxed{-2}
\]
